Generate NanoIDs and Sqids

Source: R/generate-text.R
id_nanoid.Rd

id_nanoid() generates NanoIDs: size symbols drawn uniformly from alphabet, by NanoID 6's customRandom(). Random bytes come in batches, each read from its last byte, and a byte at or above the largest multiple of the alphabet's size below 256 is rejected, so every symbol is equally likely. When rejection uses up a batch, another is drawn.

Usage

id_nanoid(n = 1, size = 21, alphabet = NULL, random = NULL)

id_sqids(numbers, alphabet = NULL, min_length = 0, blocklist = NULL)

Arguments

n

The number of NanoIDs.

size

Symbols per NanoID, 21 by default.

alphabet

The symbols, or NULL for the format's default: A-Za-z0-9_- for NanoID and a-zA-Z0-9 for Sqids. 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters for NanoID, 3 to 255 for Sqids, all distinct.

random

For id_nanoid(), NULL to draw from the operating system, or a raw vector read batch by batch, for reproducible values; running out is a zuid_type_error.

numbers

A numeric vector, or a list of numeric vectors, of whole numbers from 0 to 2^53 - 1. NA or NULL gives NA.

min_length

The shortest Sqid, 0 to 255.

blocklist

NULL for the default blocklist, or a character vector of words to avoid (character() for none).

Value

A zuid vector.

Details

id_sqids() encodes non-negative whole numbers as Sqids, by the specification's algorithm: the default alphabet and blocklist unless given, and padded to min_length. A numeric vector gives one Sqid per number; a list gives one per element, encoding all its numbers. An ID that contains a blocklisted word is re-encoded with the next offset; when every offset is blocked, the result is a zuid_encode_error.

Examples

id_nanoid(2)
#> <zuid_nanoid[2]>
#> [1] 0uBITUfLdFjTDCPnyHLbA 0gFj5uA9g3OfoEE1lmMA3
id_nanoid(2, size = 10, alphabet = "0123456789abcdef")
#> <zuid_nanoid[2]>
#> [1] a69b01cb84 4d2a94dc09
id_sqids(c(1, 2, 3))
#> <zuid_sqids[3]>
#> [1] Uk gb Ef
id_sqids(list(c(1, 2, 3)), min_length = 10)
#> <zuid_sqids[1]>
#> [1] 86Rf07xd4z
